contracts.commit_point: tool_context.state[key] = value at state_tools.py:40 — the rejected key conditions must never reach this line.
contracts.declared_mechanism: In-tool validation inside set_user_state: (1) a prefix check that returns an error dict for any key not starting with 'user:' (state_tools.py:28-32); (2) a blocklist check against PROTECTED_STATE_KEYS that returns an error dict for 'user:name'/'user:email' (state_tools.py:34-38, keys defined at state_tools.py:16-19). The agent instruction restates the identity-key prohibition at prompt level (agent.py:45-46), but the code checks are the enforcing mechanism.
contracts.forbidden_condition: A set_user_state invocation whose key is 'user:name' or 'user:email' (the PROTECTED_STATE_KEYS set) or whose key does not start with 'user:' passing the in-tool checks and reaching the state write.
pending_binding_information: Whether tool_context.state mutations in this deployment are persisted by the session service to a database (app/services/adk_service is not supplied); if so, a second commit point in the database stratum may exist and would warrant a separate contract.

Whether any registered callback (log_before_tool/log_after_tool, agent.py:56-57) independently enforces the key policy; the callback implementations in app.agents.callbacks are not supplied and the file comments describe them only as logging.
contracts.protected_operation: Agent-dispatched update of user-scoped session state via the set_user_state tool, i.e., setting an allowed 'user:'-prefixed preference key to a new string value.
contracts.protected_resource: ADK ToolContext session state — specifically the auth-owned identity keys 'user:name' and 'user:email' (sourced from the authenticated user record when seeding session state, chat.py:35-38) and the 'user:'-scoped key namespace managed by the tool.
contracts.protection_obligation: The set_user_state ADK tool, registered on the production root agent, must reject any write targeting an auth-owned identity key ('user:name' or 'user:email') or any key lacking the 'user:' prefix before the value is committed to tool_context.state. (Merged from the two reviewer opinions, which state the same obligation with the second adding the production-root-agent registration binding.)
scope_limits: The guard applies only to writes attempted through the set_user_state tool; other state writes, such as seeding 'user:name'/'user:email' via build_user_state at session creation (chat.py:30-40, 73-77), are outside this guard and are the legitimate path for those keys.
The prompt-level agent instruction (agent.py:39-48) is recorded as declared intent only and is not treated as an enforcing mechanism.
Only the in-process ToolContext.state commit is asserted; any downstream persistence of that state by the session service (e.g., into a database) is not established from the supplied source.

Authentication of the chat endpoint (get_current_user, chat.py:47) is ordinary web auth and out of scope; chat.py:91-95 is cited solely as the dataflow binding the agent run — and thus tool dispatch — to the production request path.

missing_information: The session service implementation (imported at chat.py:24 from app.services.adk_service) is not supplied, so whether the ToolContext.state write at state_tools.py:40 is subsequently persisted to a database cannot be confirmed from the supplied lines; only the in-process session-state commit is evidenced.

Implementations of app.agents.callbacks (log_before_tool, log_after_tool, etc., imported at agent.py:12 and registered at agent.py:54-59) are not supplied; whether any lifecycle callback adds independent enforcement of the key policy is unknown.

No supplied source shows the ADK framework's tool-dispatch internals, so how tool arguments produced by the model reach set_user_state (and whether any framework-level validation applies before the in-tool checks) is not evidenced; this does not affect the in-tool guard itself but limits precise characterization of the dispatch path.
